summary: Iteration 29 targeted re-verification of iteration 28's two reported bugs — both PASS. (A) Anonymous lockout UX: /api/auth/anonymous, /api/auth/me and /api/auth/login now all return the user with an explicit is_anonymous boolean derived server-side by _public_user() in server.py:307. Frontend AuthContext.normalizeUser also defensively enforces it. Navigating to /messages as an anonymous user now correctly shows the 'ACCESSO BLOCCATO' lock screen with the Italian body 'La chat è disponibile solo per gli utenti registrati…'; /messages/user_16f709708760 shows 'Accesso non consentito' with no composer and no crash; bottom tab bar still shows the Messaggi icon. (B) No duplicate bubble after send: logged in as chat_a@test.it, opened chat with chat_b, sent two distinct messages ('TEST_dedupe1_…' and 'TEST_dedupe2_…') 3.5s apart — each appears exactly once in the DOM, no 'tmp_' ids linger, ZERO 'two children with the same key' warnings, ZERO console errors. (C) Regression sanity: POST /api/messages/send, GET /api/messages/conversations, POST /api/users/{chat_b_id}/report all return 200; /user/user_16f709708760 renders the red INVIA MESSAGGIO CTA and ⋮ menu (testIDs user-send-message and user-menu). Fragment onLayout warning previously reported is no longer observed (ListEmptyComponent now wrapped in <View>). Pytest: 5/5 targeted checks pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration29_verify.py.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _public_user (line 301) — good: single point of truth normalizing is_anonymous for ALL auth-shaped responses.

AuthContext.normalizeUser is a nice belt-and-suspenders guard on the client; keeps guards throughout the app (messages/index.tsx, MessagingContext, NotificationsContext, user/[id].tsx) correct even if a future endpoint forgets the field.

messages/[userId].tsx send handler (lines 190-199): de-dupes by message_id when the WS 'message.new/sent' echo arrives before the HTTP response, and cleans the temp bubble if the API call fails. Solid.
server.py is now 3842 lines — still worth extracting the messaging block into a dedicated router in a future refactor (previously noted, non-blocking).
